title: Choose the visual world for Flock Together
question: Re-rolled against your steer: playful, colorful, sheep and pasture. The roll assigned Paddock Rotation. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll again.

options.label: Paddock Rotation
options.lineage: Aerial farmland mosaics, grazing-rotation plans, five-bar gates, raddle marking dye
options.thesis: The screen is a working paddock map seen from above, so a majority is not a bar chart but the paddock the flock actually crowded into.
options.viewport: A full-bleed aerial mosaic of paddocks in saturated grass green, chartreuse and gold stubble, carved up by thick near-black hedgerows. A hazard-yellow gate-sign bar across the top carries the name, the room code as a lot number and a 9-paddock rotation strip. The question stands mid-field on a white enamel sign, and a five-bar galvanised gate swings shut across the paddock mouth as monumental countdown numerals run down. Your flock waits at the gate as one sheep token per player: plain white fleece until you answer, then sprayed with a bright raddle mark.
options.risk: An aerial map can read as an infographic rather than a game if the field colours are timid or the sheep tokens get small, and cute-farm slides into children's-app the moment the type stops being bold and grown-up.
options.case: Every single game state already has a real artifact in this world: paddocks sized by headcount for groups, a gate closing for the timer, a sheepdog outrun covering the clustering wait, a rosette pinned on the winner, and a grazing record sheet for the scoreboard. Nothing has to be invented as chrome.

options.label: Miniature Pasture Room
options.lineage: Cyworld minihompy: furnishable isometric miniature space, acorn economy, visitor ledger
options.thesis: The pasture is a tiny isometric room you decorate, and the flock is a set of sticker sheep you watch huddle together.
options.viewport: A pastel isometric pasture held whole in frame, sticker sheep placed on it, with compact rounded label panels and a visitor-ledger column beside it.
options.case: Wins the playful-and-colourful axis outright — this is its home turf, and sticker sheep huddling in an isometric field is a direct render of the mechanic. But its grammar is pastel with soft outlines and small honest chrome, which is the weakest possible contrast for a display downscaled inside a Zoom window, and it has no native language at all for a countdown or a ranked tally.
options.risk: Lowest contrast of the three at screenshare scale, and cute enough to read as a children's app to a room of adults.

options.label: Crisis Wall
options.lineage: Nineties mecha-anime command centre: phosphor orange on absolute black, hazard chevrons, seven-segment countdowns
options.thesis: The round is a countdown emergency, with the room's answers filling condition bars toward a limit.
options.viewport: A black wall flooded orange: seven-segment digits taller than a person counting down, hazard chevrons crawling the border, framed label blocks fed by leader lines from a central schematic.
options.case: The best mechanics on the table by a clear margin — monumental seven-segment countdowns and severity-filled condition bars are exactly the timer and tally this game needs, and I have deliberately borrowed the monumental-numeral idea into the assigned direction rather than lose it. But phosphor-on-absolute-black in an alarm register contradicts both halves of your steer, and your pin binds me.
options.risk: Wrong world and wrong emotional register: an alarm wall is the opposite of a farm, and darkest of all options on a shared screen.

options.label: Alphabet Storm
options.lineage: Letters as weather: type condensing into words, breaking into storm, reshaping the ground
options.thesis: Typed answers behave as matter, condensing into a single mass where the room agrees and scattering as spent rain where it does not.
options.viewport: A wide white field where the round's answers gather as black letterforms, kerning loosening into wind before they condense into groups.
options.case: Real creative merit and the one direction where the answers themselves are the visual material rather than tokens standing in for them. But its palette grammar is paper-white and storm-black by definition, which fights colourful, there is no pasture anywhere in it, and like the room it has no countdown or tally of its own.
options.risk: Monochrome by construction, so satisfying your colour steer means breaking the world's own rules.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: What a party game screen ships: rounded geometric sans, saturated purple-to-magenta gradient, bouncy card flips, confetti on the winner — with a cartoon sheep mascot bolted on.
canonCard.viewport: Centred question card on a gradient field, answer tiles in a responsive grid, a circular countdown ring, confetti burst at reveal.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other phone-joins-the-TV game, but instantly legible to anyone who has played one.
